resources.string: How odor becomes a brain signal
An educational view of smell. Colors distinguish signals, not concentrations or sensitivity.
Inhalation brings odor into the nose
Inhaled air carries odor molecules. Only some airflow reaches the olfactory region high in the nasal cavity.
Odor molecules enter a thin mucus layer and approach cilia extending from olfactory sensory neurons.
Receptors turn chemistry into a signal
Odor molecules activate some receptors on the cilia and change the electrical activity of sensory neurons. The signal traveling onward is neural.
Sensory axons pass through openings in the cribriform plate and converge in glomeruli of the olfactory bulb. Odor molecules do not travel into the brain along this route.
Different odors can activate different combinations of olfactory channels. The bulb sends processed signals to the olfactory cortex and related regions.
How sweetness becomes a taste signal
An example of sweetness signaling in type II taste cells. Sour and salty pathways are not shown.
Dissolved molecules can reach taste-bud openings in tongue papillae. Taste does not follow a fixed map of the tongue.
Sweet molecules pass through the taste pore and reach microvilli at the tips of taste cells.
Sweet receptors activate a type II cell
Sweet molecules activate matching receptors. The cell signaling that follows produces electrical activity in a type II taste cell.
Electrical activity opens ATP release channels in the type II cell. ATP reaches nearby gustatory nerve endings.
ATP activates receptors on the gustatory nerve endings. Neural signals travel to the brainstem and are processed centrally.
ATP release for sweet, bitter and umami (mouse study)
How light touch becomes a nerve signal
An example of light touch through the Merkel cell and nerve ending. Pressure and firing are qualitative, not a sensory test.
Contact slightly indents the skin. This deformation reaches the receptors underneath.
Merkel cells near the base of the epidermis sit beside sensory nerve endings. Both contribute to light touch.
Deformation can open mechanosensitive channels such as PIEZO2, allowing ions in and changing electrical activity.
A steady press can keep signaling
During a steady press, this receptor complex can continue signaling, with a pattern different from initial contact.
When the object moves away, deformation fades and neural activity returns toward its earlier level.
How the inner ear senses motion and steadies gaze
An educational model of motion and reflexes. Directions and displacements are illustrative, not personal readings.
Three differently oriented canals detect head rotation in different planes. The otolith organs detect linear acceleration and tilt relative to gravity.
Fluid lags when the head turns
As the head starts turning, the walls move with it. Endolymph lags relative to the walls because of inertia.
The cupula bends the hair bundles
Endolymph deflects the flexible cupula and bends hair bundles. The bending direction affects the vestibular nerve signal.
Otolith organs detect tilt and acceleration
During tilt or linear acceleration, the weighted otolith membrane moves relative to sensory cells and bends their hair bundles.
Vestibular signals through brainstem circuits rotate the eyes in the opposite direction, briefly keeping gaze on a target.
Human semicircular canals and gaze reflex
